title: Keep one reveal for the end
description: Hold one fact until the last line, and say why the story needed it there.
oneStarDescription: Write the fact you will hold.
twoStarDescription: Tell the story so it still makes sense before the last line.
threeStarDescription: Say the fact in the last line and ask whether it arrived too late to follow.

title: Keep the label in the crop
description: Crop a photo and keep a label readable in the frame.
oneStarDescription: Point to the label that must stay.
twoStarDescription: Crop the photo and show the label still readable.
threeStarDescription: Show one crop you rejected because the label was cut, if you made one.

title: Label left and right on a photo
description: Label the left and right of a photo from the viewer's side, and say whose left you mean.
oneStarDescription: Write whether you mean the viewer's left or the subject's left.
twoStarDescription: Mark that side on a copy.
threeStarDescription: Ask someone to point to the side you named.

title: Label the one change
description: Show two images in the same frame and label the one thing that changed.
oneStarDescription: Take or draw two views with the same edges.
twoStarDescription: Change one thing and label it on the second image.
threeStarDescription: Ask someone what changed, and fix the label if they name something else.

title: Leave a note in their words
description: Leave a short note using words the person chose for what they need.
oneStarDescription: Ask what the note should say.
twoStarDescription: Write those words, not a paraphrase they did not hear.
threeStarDescription: Read it back and change it if they ask.

title: Leave a path to the door
description: Leave a clear path from the seats to the door, and show it to one person.
oneStarDescription: Walk from a seat to the door without moving a chair.
twoStarDescription: Move one thing that blocked the path, if you may.
threeStarDescription: Ask one person to walk it and say whether they had to turn sideways.

title: Leave a prop for the next person
description: Leave one object and a one-line note so the next person can continue a scene.
oneStarDescription: Pick one object and write what it is in the story.
twoStarDescription: Write one line the next person can use.
threeStarDescription: Watch them add one beat, and do not correct them unless they ask.

title: List what stays
description: List two things that will stay the same, then change one other thing.
oneStarDescription: Write two things you will not change.
twoStarDescription: Change one other thing only.
threeStarDescription: Show that the two stayed.

title: Listen for an echo
description: Clap once in two places and say where you heard the clap come back.
oneStarDescription: Clap once and say whether you heard a repeat.
twoStarDescription: Clap once in a second place and compare.
threeStarDescription: Say where the repeat was clearer, or that you heard none.

title: Log a mistake and its cue
description: Write three mistakes you made on a task and the cue that would have stopped each one.
oneStarDescription: Write three mistakes from one piece of work.
twoStarDescription: Beside each, write the cue that would have stopped it.
threeStarDescription: On the next try, use one of those cues and say whether the mistake returned.

title: Make a readable name card
description: Write a name large enough to read from the other side of a table.
oneStarDescription: Write the name the person asked you to use.
twoStarDescription: Read it from the other side of the table, or ask someone to.
threeStarDescription: Rewrite one card that failed the test.

title: Make the heading the only large type
description: Make one heading visibly larger than the body, and leave the body one size.
oneStarDescription: Write the body in one size.
twoStarDescription: Make one heading larger and nothing else.
threeStarDescription: Ask someone where their eye went first.

title: Mark a claim and an example
description: Mark which sentence states the claim and which sentence is only an example.
oneStarDescription: Underline the sentence that says what the piece wants you to accept.
twoStarDescription: Mark a different sentence as an example and write what it is an example of.
threeStarDescription: Give the marked page to someone else and ask them to point to the claim.

title: Mark a guess about a place name
description: Read a street or room name and write what it might refer to, marked as a guess.
oneStarDescription: Copy the name as signed.
twoStarDescription: Write what it might refer to, with the word guess.
threeStarDescription: Write where you would look to check it, or that you do not know.

title: Mark a judging word
description: Mark one word that judges and one word that only describes.
oneStarDescription: Underline one word that says what is there.
twoStarDescription: Underline one word that praises, blames, or ranks, and say so.
threeStarDescription: Write the same sentence with the judging word replaced by a description.

title: Mark a line tools will not cross
description: Mark a line on the table and keep tools on the work side of it.
oneStarDescription: Put a tape or a pencil line where tools should stop.
twoStarDescription: Do a small task and keep tools on one side.
threeStarDescription: Show whether any tool crossed, and put it back if it did.

title: Mark a puddle and return
description: Mark the edge of a puddle and note later the same day whether it is smaller.
oneStarDescription: Mark the edge with a stick or a note, without damaging the place.
twoStarDescription: Return later and say whether the edge has moved.
threeStarDescription: Write whether the spot was in sun or shade.

title: Mark a rest while you clap
description: Clap a short pattern that includes a silence you can point to.
oneStarDescription: Clap a pattern of a few beats.
twoStarDescription: Leave one silence and point to it.
threeStarDescription: Ask someone to clap it back, including the silence.

title: Mark three sounds on a line
description: Draw a short walk as a line and mark three sounds where you heard them.
oneStarDescription: Draw the walk with a start and an end.
twoStarDescription: Mark three sounds at the place on the line where you heard them.
threeStarDescription: Walk or recall the line and say whether the order matches.

title: Mark which answer used the notes
description: Write three questions, answer them, and mark which answer used the notes.
oneStarDescription: Write three questions about one page.
twoStarDescription: Answer them, and mark the one that needed the notes.
threeStarDescription: Answer the same three later without the notes and say which you lost.

title: Measure one plant and date it
description: Measure one plant against a ruler and write the date.
oneStarDescription: Write the height you measured and where you put the ruler.
twoStarDescription: Write the date beside the number.
threeStarDescription: Measure again on a later day and say what changed, or that you have not returned yet.

title: Mend a tear from the back
description: Mend a torn page from the back so the text on the front stays readable.
oneStarDescription: Put the tape or tissue on the back of a scrap or a page you may mend.
twoStarDescription: Show that the words on the front can still be read.
threeStarDescription: Trim tape that covers a word, or say you need a thinner mend.

title: Move a finished draft aside
description: Move a draft you are finished with into a place you named, and leave a working file separate.
oneStarDescription: Write the folder or envelope for finished drafts.
twoStarDescription: Move the finished draft there.
threeStarDescription: Show the file you are still changing, separate from the finished one.

title: Name a backup person
description: Name who will do a job and who will do it if that person is late.
oneStarDescription: Write the person for one job.
twoStarDescription: Write a second person and tell them.
threeStarDescription: Write the moment the backup should step in.

title: Name a loud and a soft moment
description: In a piece of music or a room, name one louder moment and one softer moment.
oneStarDescription: Point to a moment that is louder than what is around it.
twoStarDescription: Point to a softer moment.
threeStarDescription: Say what you compared them with.

title: Name one absence
description: Name one fact, person, or group a short piece does not mention, and why that matters to the claim.
oneStarDescription: Write the claim in your own sentence.
twoStarDescription: Name one thing the piece would need to mention for you to follow the claim.
threeStarDescription: Say how that absence changes what you can conclude, in one sentence.

title: Name one dating clue
description: Name one visible clue that places an old photo in time, and the limit of that clue.
oneStarDescription: Point to one thing in the photo you are using.
twoStarDescription: Say the range of time that clue suggests.
threeStarDescription: Write one reason the clue could mislead you.

title: Name the audience of a poster
description: Say who a poster is speaking to, using the words and the place it hangs.
oneStarDescription: Point to the words that name or imply a reader.
twoStarDescription: Say how the place it hangs supports or limits that guess.
threeStarDescription: Write the audience as a guess if the poster does not name them.

title: Name the idea you oppose
description: Say the idea you disagree with and one reason, without a remark about the person.
oneStarDescription: Write the idea in words they would recognize.
twoStarDescription: Add one reason that is about the idea.
threeStarDescription: Read it and delete any comment about their character.

title: Name the missing piece
description: Name the piece you are missing and the place you already looked.
oneStarDescription: Write the name of the piece you do not have.
twoStarDescription: Write the places you already looked for it.
threeStarDescription: Ask for the piece using its name and where you looked.

title: Name the next speaker
description: Stop and name the person who has the next turn.
oneStarDescription: Stop at the end of your point.
twoStarDescription: Say their name and that the turn is theirs.
threeStarDescription: Do not add a second point while they start.

title: Name the wind by a landmark
description: Write where the wind came from by pointing to a landmark, not a guessed degree.
oneStarDescription: Face the wind and name the landmark it comes from.
twoStarDescription: Write the landmark and the time.
threeStarDescription: Check again a little later and say whether it still matches.

title: Name tomorrow's practice
description: Write the one thing you will practice next, and where you will do it.
oneStarDescription: Write one action, not a topic.
twoStarDescription: Write where and roughly when.
threeStarDescription: After that time, write whether you did it.

title: Name what you will leave
description: Name one thing you could take and then leave it where it is.
oneStarDescription: Point to the thing and say you will leave it.
twoStarDescription: Show it still there when you go.
threeStarDescription: Write one reason it stays, such as a rule or a living plant.

title: Name who changed the decision
description: Say whose point changed a decision, in front of the people who were there.
oneStarDescription: Say the point that changed the decision.
twoStarDescription: Say who brought that point.
threeStarDescription: Repeat the decision so the credit does not replace it.

title: Name who is quoted
description: Name the person whose words appear as a quote and the person who wrote the surrounding text.
oneStarDescription: Point to the quoted words and to the name attached to them.
twoStarDescription: Write the name of the person quoted and the name of the person who wrote the piece, or note which one is missing.
threeStarDescription: Find the next place that quote is attributed, or write that you cannot find it.

title: Note a repair on an old object
description: Point to a repair on an old object and say what the repair tells you and what it does not.
oneStarDescription: Point to the mend, patch, or replaced part.
twoStarDescription: Say what the repair shows about use.
threeStarDescription: Say one thing the repair stops you from knowing about the original.

title: Note which way a tree leans
description: Note which way a tree leans and what stands beside it.
oneStarDescription: Name a landmark you can use as a direction.
twoStarDescription: Write which way the trunk leans relative to that landmark.
threeStarDescription: Write what is beside the trunk, such as a wall or an open side.

title: Note open and closed blooms
description: Note which blooms on one plant are open and which are closed at two times of day.
oneStarDescription: Write the time and what is open.
twoStarDescription: Write a later time and what changed.
threeStarDescription: Show that you did not pick a bloom for the note.

title: Note the light on a color sample
description: Label a color sample with the light you viewed it in.
oneStarDescription: Look at the sample in one light and name that light.
twoStarDescription: Write the light on the sample or its note.
threeStarDescription: Look at it in a second light and say whether you would still call it the same.
